AUTHOR: Papadaki C
TITLE: Unlocking flow-habitat relationships in mountain rivers of Epirus, Greece using object detection and hydrodynamic simulation
SPECIES: fish (single class; river dominated by West Balkan trout Salmo farioides)
DATA: Own stereo underwater video from pool-riffle transition zones, Sept-Oct 2022; 144 annotated images
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'Data collection occurred during daytime with clear visibility, with the cameras positioned perpendicular to the flow' (visibility not measured)
D_EV: Sec. 3.3: 'We used K = 5 different partitions of the dataset ... divided into three subsets of training, validation and test data with the proportions of 60 %, 20 % and 20 %'
R_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'the use of a limited training set due to the 60–20-20 split' — single river dataset only
C_EV: no statement found (confidence scores only shown in Fig. 4; no threshold value reported)
E_EV: Table 1: 'Mean values and 95 % confidence interval for various augmentation strategies on YOLO and Faster R-CNN models' (P, R, F1, mAP50, mAP50-95)
ARCH: YOLOv8 and Faster R-CNN; augmentation study (flip, blur, affine); coupled conceptually with HEC-RAS 2D hydrodynamic model and habitat suitability curves
METR: Precision, recall, F1, mAP50, mAP50-95 (mean and 95% CI over 5 partitions)
NOTE: Habitat suitability curves/WUA are derived from MANUAL videogrammetry observations (FEMPs measured in VidSync), not from the detector output, so E1 = 없음. V_ALL coded N under policy P1 (field sampling restricted to daytime clear visibility, visibility not measured), although depth (~1 m), daytime illumination and camera-fish distance zones (0.2-4.5 m) are reported and the text elsewhere calls the environment turbid — alternative reading V_ALL = P; verifier should check. Split unit not stated; 144 images drawn from videos, coded 이미지/프레임 무작위. 'Part of the data is openly available on GitHub' (DSHR 공개, partial).
